answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by a scarce, nontransferable proof-of-personhood credential issued after an in-person check and renewed at dawn through a liveness challenge. The credential acts as an anchor: one person can authorize only one active identity, and peers reject votes or payouts without a valid, unspent credential. An attacker must recruit real people or repeatedly defeat the check, paying for coordination and risking detection; merely spawning agents to wander across accounts gains no extra influence.
